rv.q: But they surely deserve to be articulated with more dramatic force than this.
This is a worthwhile piece of theatre, certainly, though one that feels more like an invitation to further reading than an entirely satisfying piece of drama.
What emerges is an abstraction of something that is, admittedly, hard in more ways than one to envisage.
Pascal achieves nuance for the most part, allowing space for contradictions to be true at the same time without lecturing.
Instead, it feels like a mash-up driven at a relentlessly tight pace with little breathing space, leaving little to linger in either the mind or the heart.

cn.t: Critics find Pascal's exploration of Hannah Arendt's internment at Camp Gurs well-intentioned but uneven, with a muddled message and stiff staging undermining the compelling historical subject matter.
